A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StructTuning study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original LongBench and MMedBench evaluations, corpus-scaling experiments and component/data-synthesis ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains original evaluations and adds larger-corpus experiments, general-capability measurements, SCPT ablations and retrieval analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The hierarchy extraction, conditional SCPT with structure replay, and structure-guided SSFT synthesis and response formats remain unchanged. V3 documents additional implementation details and tests alternative components through ablations without adopting a revised method.

E1.justification: V3 adds general-capability evaluation on MMLU, C-Eval, TruthfulQA, WinoGrande and ARC_c (Table A7). It retains the seven LongBench subsets and six-language MMedBench evaluation but removes the LongBench open-book scenario from both recall and F1 comparisons.

E2.justification: V3 adds AdaptLLM and RAFT to the English-training MMedBench comparison (Table 4). It removes the LongBench open-book comparator and the InternLM-7B and InternLM2+MMed rows. The remaining InternLM2 and Llama2 results are retained through relocated tables.

E3.justification: V3 extends the 30M/76M/132M corpus experiments with 250M and 1.2B budgets and adds controlled SCPT and RAG parameter experiments. Appendix A.2 replaces random corpus sampling with document-length-based selection. Section 4.1 changes the stated LongBench training corpus from 10,476 passages to 14K; this establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds template-diversity, hierarchy-level and loss-masking ablations (B.5), general-capability retention checks (B.3), RAG parameter/retrieval analyses and a failure example (B.7), and synthetic/test overlap measurements (A.1). It also extends the existing scaling analysis. The earlier extraction-model and SFT-synthesis ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed counts, repeated-run aggregation, error bars or formal significance tests for their evaluations. V3's two fixed-template variants are distinct ablation settings; the confidence intervals appearing in Figure A3 belong to retrieved medical text.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports 67.74% average MMedBench accuracy for Llama3 with 1.2B tokens, alongside the retained 67.75% MMed comparator and 65.36% result at 76M (Table 2). It adds baseline, general-capability, overlap and ablation results. Retained closed-book LongBench scores are unchanged, while open-book results and two medical comparator rows disappear.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), including conditional modeling, hierarchy recall and the fitted scaling expressions, remain mathematically unchanged. The new terminology explanations and empirical alternative-loss discussion introduce no substantive formal assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The headline changes from achieving roughly half the traditional injection gain with 0.3% of the corpus to matching that gain with approximately 5%. V2 presented the latter endpoint as an unverified potential; v3 asserts its experimental achievement and adds explicit superiority claims against AdaptLLM and RAFT. The underlying SCPT/SSFT contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning template diversity, hierarchy levels, general-capability retention and retrieval failures. It argues that smaller models can synthesize the grounded QA data. The limitations paragraph replaces v2's unverified-scaling emphasis with preprocessing and synthesis overhead, while earlier explanations involving incomplete medical-corpus coverage are removed.

D1.justification: V3 supplies the full 20-template SCPT pool, a 3072-token medical chunk limit, extracted-structure statistics and detailed RAG implementation information, including BGE-M3, LlamaIndex and default retrieval settings. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v2's explicit LongBench cosine scheduler and medical SFT learning rate are omitted.

R1.justification: V3 adds substantive comparisons with AdaptLLM and RAFT and a dedicated conditional-language-modeling discussion explaining SCPT's relationship to the already-cited CTRL and to system prompts. References and discussion expand into retrieval, parameter-efficient tuning and coding, while LawGPT is dropped. The original structured-knowledge positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work summary and experimental narrative undergo extensive compression and rewriting. Detailed related work moves into Appendix C, several existing analyses move to Appendix B, and terminology explanations are added. The author list and equal-contribution statement also change.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout, combines the knowledge-structure illustration and SCPT template into Figure 3, expands the scaling plot and reorganizes the medical comparison tables. It relocates existing displays and adds multiple analysis tables, a path/branch diagram, a retrieval example and the full template-pool figure.

improvement.justification: V2 explicitly left its central 5%-corpus prediction unverified; v3 supplies a 1.2B-token experiment reaching 67.74% accuracy versus 67.75% for the 25.5B-token MMed comparator (Table 2). Added competing methods, component ablations and retrieval checks substantially strengthen validation. Removed comparators, inconsistent data descriptions and overconfident interpretations of the limited general-capability results weaken auditability, but do not outweigh the stronger evidence for the central data-efficiency claim.
